theme: Booking.com datasets beyond the 515k reviews: listing/price snapshots, alternative-accommodation counts, Booking scrapers, WSDM/RecSys Booking challenge data
queries_run: gh search repos "booking.com dataset hotels" --sort stars
gh search repos "booking challenge recsys" --sort stars
gh search repos "hotel-id booking dataset alternative accommodation" --sort stars
gh search repos "multi-destination trips booking" --sort stars

candidates.name: ZoranPandovski/BookingScraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scraper for Booking.com hotel search-result pages (name, price, rating, location). No committed dataset, but 100 stars and updated as recently as 6 Sep 2026, so an actively maintained method exists. GPL-3.0.
candidates.why_useful: Could be adapted to build a repeated, point-in-time Booking.com price/availability panel analogous to the Inside Airbnb calendar captures — useful as a competitor-supply/price cross-check, addresses gap #9 (competitor and adjacent supply).
candidates.time_coverage: point-in-time scrape only, no historical archive

candidates.name: gilbertekalea/booking.com_crawler
candidates.what_it_holds: Scraper collecting Booking.com property name, review score, price, address, plus image/URL download. No dataset committed. MIT licence, 18 stars, updated 6 Sep 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Same class as BookingScraper — a method to build a fresh Booking.com price/rating panel; would need a human ToS decision before running per repo rules.

candidates.name: Edioff/booking-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Async Playwright-based Booking.com scraper: multi-city search, detail extraction, pricing, amenities, reviews, with anti-bot handling. MIT, 3 stars, updated Aug 2026.
candidates.why_useful: More technically capable scraper (handles anti-bot measures, multi-city) than the simpler BeautifulSoup scripts; if a repeated price panel were ever authorized this is a more robust starting point.

candidates.name: omkarcloud/booking-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Booking.com scraper extracting hotels with live prices, availability, ratings, reviews to structured JSON; markets itself as avoiding blocks/proxies. Updated Aug 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Another scraping method option for a Booking.com price panel; no data committed.

candidates.name: pixelcrash/Sync-Rentals-Calendar
candidates.what_it_holds: Self-hosted tool to synchronize iCal rental-availability calendars across Airbnb, Booking.com, and other platforms. No committed dataset — it is calendar-sync infrastructure a host would run, not a data mirror.
candidates.why_useful: Illustrates that Booking.com (and other STR/OTA platforms) expose iCal calendar feeds per-listing similar to Airbnb's; conceptually this is the mechanism by which one could build a Booking.com occupancy/availability panel analogous to Inside Airbnb calendars, addressing gaps #2 (realised occupancy) and #9, but requires a host's private iCal URLs, not a public bulk source.

candidates.name: nashmans/R-Booking.com-Data-analysis-and-NLP
candidates.what_it_holds: R project doing analysis/NLP on a Booking.com dataset the author webscraped with BeautifulSoup/Selenium; description mentions pricing dynamics and trends. Need to inspect repo contents to confirm whether the scraped CSV itself is committed (not verified beyond description) — 2 stars, updated Jan 2025.
candidates.why_useful: If the underlying scraped price/review dataset is actually committed in the repo, it would be a small independent Booking.com price snapshot rather than just a scraper; flagged for a closer look rather than a confirmed finding.
candidates.geography: unclear (likely a Europe/UK sample based on 'R' naming convention, unverified)
candidates.size_hint: unverified — description implies a scraped dataset exists but contents not confirmed

candidates.name: Asifmehdiyev/Booking_Time_Series_Modelling
candidates.what_it_holds: Repo doing time-series analysis/forecasting on what it calls a 'Booking com dataset'. Contents not verified (0 stars) — could be the well-known Portugal hotel-booking-demand dataset (which we already hold per CONTEXT.md) rather than anything new; flagged only for completeness.
candidates.why_useful: Possible duplicate of the Antonio/Almeida/Nunes Portugal hotel-booking demand dataset we already hold; not independently verified as new.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: likely the Portugal hotel-booking-demand dataset already held

notes: Search was noisy: the vast majority of 'booking.com' / 'booking' GitHub hits are generic booking-system web-app boilerplate (hotel/room/appointment/movie/taxi booking CRUD apps) or SEO-spam repos advertising commercial scraping APIs (e.g. wrbqkh53/booking-scraper-api, znes80/booking-scraper-api) with zero data or real code — excluded per instructions. No WSDM/RecSys 'Booking.com Challenge' (2019/2021 multi-destination trip dataset) mirror was found on GitHub; that dataset requires registration with Booking.com/WSDM and does not appear to be redistributed in any repo (competition rules likely forbid redistribution) — worth noting as a dead end rather than a gap we can fill this way. No repo was found with a genuinely novel, committed Booking.com price/listing/alternative-accommodation-count dataset beyond what CONTEXT.md already lists (515k reviews Kaggle set, RecTour24, Portugal hotel-booking-demand). The most real findings are competitor-price scraper *methods* (ZoranPandovski/BookingScraper being the most active/starred), which under repo rule #6 would need explicit human sign-off before running since they touch a live commercial site's terms of service. Suggest a future scout try Google dorking / Zenodo / Kaggle directly for 'Booking.com Hotel Booking Demand' variants and academic RecTour/WSDM papers' code-release links, since GitHub repo search itself surfaces almost no legitimate Booking.com bulk-data mirrors — likely because Booking.com's ToS explicitly prohibits scraping/redistribution, so serious researchers keep such data off GitHub (Zenodo/institutional repos instead).
